question: When can a neural network be understood as a kernel method, and when do its features change?
foundations: Lee et al., [Wide Neural Networks of Any Depth Evolve as Linear Models Under Gradient Descent](https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.06720) (2019), selected sections on Taylor linearization and squared-loss dynamics. Review Jacobians, Gram matrices and gradient flow.
main: Jacot, Gabriel & Hongler, [Neural Tangent Kernel: Convergence and Generalization in Neural Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.07572) (2018).
recent: Haas et al., [On the Surprising Effectiveness of Large Learning Rates under Standard Width Scaling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.22491) (2025).
focus: Derive function-space gradient flow and its solution for squared loss, then compare a finite network with its linearization. Use the recent paper to examine why width, parameterization, learning rate and the choice of loss matter for claims about feature learning.

question: How should initialization and updates scale as networks become wider or deeper?
foundations: Yang & Hu, [Tensor Programs IV: Feature Learning in Infinite-Width Neural Networks](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v139/yang21c.html) (2021), selected sections on parameterization and feature learning. The preceding NTK session supplies the contrasting linearized regime.
main: Yang et al., [Tensor Programs V: Tuning Large Neural Networks via Zero-Shot Hyperparameter Transfer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.03466) (NeurIPS 2021; arXiv 2022).
recent: Dey et al., [Don't Be Lazy: CompleteP Enables Compute-Efficient Deep Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.01618) (2025).
focus: Work through activation and update scaling in a small multilayer network, and inspect a learning-rate transfer experiment. Discuss the additional constraints introduced by depth; width transfer alone does not establish depth transfer or effective nonlinear learning.

question: How do recurrence, selectivity and structured matrices produce an efficient sequence model?
foundations: Gu, Goel & Ré, [Efficiently Modeling Long Sequences with Structured State Spaces](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.00396) (S4, 2021/22), selected sections on discretization and recurrence. Gu & Dao, [Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.00752) (2023), selected sections on input-dependent dynamics.
main: Dao & Gu, [Transformers Are SSMs: Generalized Models and Efficient Algorithms Through Structured State Space Duality](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/dao24a.html) (Mamba-2, 2024).
recent: Lahoti et al., [Mamba-3: Improved Sequence Modeling Using State Space Principles](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.15569) (2026).
focus: Unroll an SSM into a structured matrix and explain the restricted attention–SSM duality used by Mamba-2. Examine a state-tracking experiment from Mamba-3 and distinguish algorithmic complexity from measured hardware efficiency.

question: How can a forward pass perform learning without changing the network's parameters?
foundations: von Oswald et al., [Transformers Learn In-Context by Gradient Descent](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.07677) (2023), selected sections on the linear-attention construction. Review least squares, ridge regression and Bayesian prediction for linear models.
main: Akyürek et al., [What Learning Algorithm Is In-Context Learning? Investigations with Linear Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.15661) (2023).
recent: Wurgaft et al., [In-Context Learning Strategies Emerge Rationally](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.17859) (2025).
focus: Work through one regression-learning construction and compare gradient-descent, ridge and Bayesian predictors on a controlled task distribution. Separate existence constructions and observed behavior in trained synthetic-task models from claims about general language models.

question: What unlabeled objective makes adaptation improve the task we actually care about?
foundations: Sun, Wang, Liu, Miller, Efros & Hardt, [*Test-Time Training with Self-Supervision for Generalization under Distribution Shifts*](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/sun20b.html) (ICML 2020). Shared encoders, self-supervised auxiliary tasks and the gradient-alignment condition under the paper’s smooth/convex assumptions.
main: Durasov, Shocher, Oner, Chechik, Efros & Fua, [*IT³: Idempotent Test-Time Training*](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v267/durasov25a.html) (ICML 2025). Learn prediction feedback and use consistency between successive predictions as the test-time objective.
recent: IT³ is the recent anchor. Supplementary resources: [arXiv paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.04201) and [official implementation](https://github.com/nikitadurasov/ittt). Compare its idempotence-based consistency objective with the original TTT auxiliary-task design.
focus: Derive the original gradient-alignment argument and IT³ consistency loss, then inspect an adaptation experiment and a failure case. IT³ requires its own training setup; discuss when consistency can be uninformative and how to stop adaptation.

topic: Test-time training: learning as neural memory
question: How can parameter updates store context, and how should training prepare a model to learn at inference?
foundations: Ba et al., [*Using Fast Weights to Attend to the Recent Past*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.06258) (2016). Fast versus slow weights and associative memory; recap the original Sun et al. TTT formulation.
main: Sun et al., [*Learning to (Learn at Test Time): RNNs with Expressive Hidden States*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.04620) (2024). A model is the recurrent hidden state, and self-supervised gradient updates are the state transition.
recent: Tandon et al., [*End-to-End Test-Time Training for Long Context*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.23675) (2025). Next-token updates compress context into weights, with a meta-learned initialization.
focus: Work through a TTT-Linear update and its recurrent computation. Compare layer-local reconstruction with end-to-end next-token adaptation; distinguish sequence memory from adapting to a shifted test distribution.

question: Can a network generate the parameters another network needs for a new task or context?
foundations: Ha, Dai & Le, [HyperNetworks](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.09106) (2016/17). Hu et al., [LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.09685) (2021/22), selected sections on low-rank parameter updates.
recent: Charakorn et al., [Doc-to-LoRA: Learning to Instantly Internalize Contexts](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.15902) (2026).
focus: Explain the conditioning signal, generated low-rank update and training objective, then examine a held-out-task or document experiment. Compare the cost and information limits of generated adaptation with fine-tuning and keeping the original context available.

question: When does prediction in representation space support understanding, dynamics and planning?
foundations: Assran et al., [Self-Supervised Learning from Images with a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture](https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.08243) (I-JEPA, 2023), selected sections on masking, target representations and collapse prevention.
main: Assran et al., [V-JEPA 2: Self-Supervised Video Models Enable Understanding, Prediction and Planning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09985) (2025).
recent: Maes et al., [LeWorldModel: Stable End-to-End Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture from Pixels](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19312) (2026).
focus: Trace the representation-prediction objective and action-conditioned planning loop, then analyze a planning result and its data requirements. Contrast target-network stabilization with regularizing the latent distribution; representation quality and accurate action-conditioned dynamics are separate questions.

question: Why can adding parameter updates combine capabilities, and when does task interference prevent it?
foundations: Ilharco et al., [Editing Models with Task Arithmetic](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.04089) (2023). Review parameter differences relative to a shared pretrained checkpoint and the NTK session's function-space linearization.
main: Ortiz-Jimenez, Favero & Frossard, [Task Arithmetic in the Tangent Space: Improved Editing of Pre-Trained Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.12827) (2023).
recent: Hitit, Girrbach & Akata, [A Systematic Study of In-the-Wild Model Merging for Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.21437) (2025 preprint; TMLR 2026).
focus: Derive how adding task vectors affects a linearized model and examine the proposed weight-disentanglement mechanism. Compare controlled task combinations with heterogeneous checkpoints, including conflicting objectives and gains relative to the best individual model.

question: What is a feature, and can sparse autoencoders recover the units a network computes with?
foundations: Elhage et al., [Toy Models of Superposition](https://transformer-circuits.pub/2022/toy_model/index.html) (2022), selected sections on sparse features, interference and the two-feature toy model.
main: Templeton et al., [Scaling Monosemanticity: Extracting Interpretable Features from Claude 3 Sonnet](https://transformer-circuits.pub/2024/scaling-monosemanticity/index.html) (2024).
recent: Leask et al., [Sparse Autoencoders Do Not Find Canonical Units of Analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.04878) (2025).
focus: Explain the sparse-autoencoder objective and reproduce or analyze a small superposition experiment. Examine feature interventions alongside the stitching and meta-SAE evidence, asking whether interpretability, completeness and atomicity are being measured separately.

topic: Mechanistic interpretability: circuits and causal tests
question: How can we trace a model's computation and test whether the proposed explanation is causal?
foundations: Elhage et al., [A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits](https://transformer-circuits.pub/2021/framework/index.html) (2021), selected sections on the residual stream and attention's QK/OV decomposition. The preceding features session supplies sparse representations.
main: Ameisen et al., [Circuit Tracing: Revealing Computational Graphs in Language Models](https://transformer-circuits.pub/2025/attribution-graphs/methods.html) (2025).
recent: Kamath et al., [Tracing Attention Computation Through Feature Interactions](https://transformer-circuits.pub/2025/attention-qk/index.html) (2025).
focus: Explain how a replacement model produces an attribution graph and work through one circuit case study with an intervention. Identify approximation errors and omitted computations, then examine what the attention extension adds to the explanation.

question: How can attraction and repulsion during training produce a one-pass generator, and when does zero drift identify the correct distribution?
foundations: Yujia Li, Swersky & Zemel, [*Generative Moment Matching Networks*](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v37/li15.html) (ICML 2015). Kernel mean embeddings, maximum mean discrepancy and distribution matching from samples.
main: Deng, He Li, Tianhong Li, Du & He, [*Generative Modeling via Drifting*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.04770) (2026). Estimate an attraction-repulsion field from real and generated samples and fit frozen drifted targets.
recent: Esteban-Casadevall et al., [*Kernel-Gradient Drifting Models*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.10727) (2026), including Max Welling. A mathematical companion for kernel-gradient fields, smoothing and distribution identifiability. [Original drifting project and demonstrations](https://lambertae.github.io/projects/drifting/).
focus: Derive the drift and regression update, including the role of stopping gradients through the target. Examine a 2D example, equilibrium assumptions and one ablation; arbitrary zero drift need not certify distribution equality.

question: Can data-to-generated nearest-neighbor matching achieve coverage and high fidelity without an iterative sampler?
foundations: Ke Li & Jitendra Malik, [*Implicit Maximum Likelihood Estimation*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.09087) (2018). Implicit distributions, nearest-neighbor assignment, mode coverage and the likelihood connection under stated assumptions.
main: Chirag Vashist & Ke Li, [*ROMS-IMLE: A Minimalist Approach to Competitive Single-Step Generative Modelling*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19332) (2026). Revisit IMLE with intermediate-resolution supervision and robust losses.
recent: ROMS-IMLE is the recent anchor. The authors’ [method page](https://serchirag.github.io/roms-imle/) provides additional explanation and experiments.
focus: Explain the direction of nearest-neighbor matching, latent assignment and alternating regression, then examine sampling cost and the ROMS-IMLE ablations. Keep the maximum-likelihood connection tied to its assumptions.
